title: Total Mission (Matthew 28:16–20)
description: Whole Church, Whole Earth: Total Mission
transcript: Good morning to all of you, and thank you for this opportunity to preach today on this Mission Sunday. Thank you, Natasha, and other leaders who invited me. Christianity is a missionary movement and a missionary religion. The Christian gospel is by its very nature good news for the whole world. All the four Gospels contain passages that portray Jesus as commissioning his disciples for this mission to the whole world. Matthew's version of the Great Commission is probably the most influential of the four, and the Church has been inspired by it again and again. My aim today is to look at this passage that was read for you through a pair of Iranian eyes and share with you what I find inspiring in it. I called my message "The Church's Total Mission" because there are 5 "alls" or totalities in this, in this passage that I am going to look at. Let's have a look at each one of these and see what lessons they have for us and our mission today. So the first one, total authority. Here we heard that Jesus told his disciples, all authority in heaven and on earth is given to me. The church's mission is a total mission because it is founded on the deep conviction about Jesus Jesus' total authority. It is the risen and victorious Lord who has received all the authority from the Father that sends us on our mission. This does not mean that Jesus did not have any authority before. Matthew himself makes it very clear on several occasions that Jesus did have great authority in his life and ministry even before his death. He had authority in his teaching and preaching. He had authority in forgiving sins. He also had authority over sickness and death and over evil spirits. He had also authority over wind and storm and sea. So he did have authority even before, but now he has received a much greater authority. His authority now is total. It is no longer limited to any specific area. Now it covers both heaven and the earth. The church's Lord, our Lord, has now absolute authority over everything. He is sitting on God's very throne, exercising God's own authority over the whole world. For me as an Iranian church leader who is working closely with the fast-growing but harshly persecuted Iranian church, this is great news. It means that Khamenei does not have absolute power in Iran. Neither do Donald Trump or Kyrill Starmer for that matter. They are all, without exception, under the authority of our Lord. They cannot control everything. The Church's life and mission are not going to be determined by their whims and wishes. Jesus, he has all the authority. Without this conviction, the Church's mission can only be an impossible an unrealistic venture. But with it, the small group of the disciples will be turning the whole world upside down. If Jesus has the absolute authority, then the Iranian church is going to flourish even under persecution and is going to transform the whole nation. If Jesus really risen from the dead and is Lord, then there is great hope for the church in England and other countries of Europe as well. So the first total is— was total authority. The second one is all nations. So Jesus is calling us to disciple all nations. He says, as we Hear it, therefore go and make disciples of all nations. The church's mission is a total mission because Jesus sends his disciples to all nations without exception. This is a fulfillment of God's promise to Abraham that he will bless him and will bless all the tribes and nations of the world through him. By Jesus' receiving total authority in all heaven and the earth, we reach a new turning point in God's plan of salvation. Till now, Jesus and his disciples had— were going to minister only among the Jews. He himself says that I have come for the lost sheep of Israel, and he had also strictly limited his disciples' ministry to the same. But now that he has received total authority, a new era has dawned, and his work has no bounds whatsoever anymore. The disciples are now sent to all nations because now Jesus is given authority over all. So his disciples, including all of us today, have the right and the mandate to go to all nations and proclaim to them the good news. We are often asked, who has given you the right to evangelize other nations who have their own religions and traditions and are happily worshiping their own gods and lords? Our answer is always that our Lord has died for all and is now risen and has authority over all. He has given us the right and the mandate to bring the good news to all nations. For almost 14 centuries, it seemed that the Muslim world were— was excluded from this blessing. Centuries of mission work among these countries did not seem to have borne much fruit. Some were even losing all hope that the Muslim nations will ever respond to the message of the gospel. But praise God, the tides are turning now. As David Garrison reported in his book some time ago, a new wind is blowing. And the House of Islam. News about many Muslims coming to Christ is coming from all over the world. But as Garrison himself says, and many testify, the eye of the storm seems to be in Iran. When I became a Christian more than 50 years ago, there were hardly more than 200 Christians from a Muslim background in Iran. But a recent survey by a secular Dutch university shows that there is about 1 million Christians living in Iran at present. Over 95% of these were former Muslims. Deep and widespread disappointment and disillusionment with the Islamic regime has made Iranians desperate for a new faith. The church's growth scared the regime so much that they shut down all Farsi speaking, as I said, since 2013. But this caused even greater and faster growth. Of course, the growth is underground, and it— but the church is spreading all over the country to the extent that now, as I said, the Iranian church is known by many to be the fastest growing church in the world. This great awakening is not limited to any specific group, but rich and poor, educated and uneducated, religious and secular, villagers and people from big cities are coming to the Lord. There is a beautiful story about an elderly lady whose son becomes a Christian. Her son was a student, and he heard about Jesus and gave his life to Christ. And at first, this elderly lady was not happy about her son becoming a Christian, but gradually she noticed that the changes in her son's life was so positive, so became interested and The son was bringing CDs and DVDs about Jesus to his mom to listen to, to watch. And after some time, she gave her life to Christ. And as she was growing in her faith, there came a time that she started praying to the Lord and wanted to serve the Lord in some way. And how can this elderly lady, she couldn't read and she couldn't write, she was illiterate. So how could she serve in a country like Iran? So after some time, God put in her heart to speak about Jesus in the public transport. So what she did was that She bought some of Matthew's Gospels and asked her friends to underline bits and pieces from the Sermon on the Mount. And so she felt that she can take these, so she was taking these pieces of Scripture to a bus and look around and find a young girl or a young boy and would sit by them. And after a couple of minutes, turned to them and says, my dear, my friend have given me this booklet, but I can't, you know, read. Can you read it for me? So, you know, in Iran, people respect elderly people. So she said, of course, of course I can do it. What is it? So she starts reading. From the Sermon on the Mount. After a couple of more minutes, she turns to her and says, my dear, my ear cannot hear very well. Can you read a little louder, please? And she said, of course. So she starts reading the Sermon on the Mount even louder. And what happens is people in the front row and the back row, they are all listening to one of the most powerful sermons in the world. And in this way, this illiterate elderly lady manages to bring many people to the Lord and ask them and give them some phone numbers so that they can get in touch and hear more about the gospel. Her weakness became her strength, and that can happen to all of us. Today. So the third, the third totality, total fellowship, this is the one that is implicit in our passage. Doesn't say all, but I can see that there because this one Jesus asks us to baptize all nations in the full fellowship of the whole Trinity, the three persons of the Father, Son, and the Holy Spirit. Baptism in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit is the central piece of our commission. This is much more than merely a rite of initiation with a Trinitarian formula attached to it. As important as baptism is as such, it signifies something much more important and central to the meaning an experience of being a Christian. Jesus is commanding his disciples to initiate all nations into a full experience of fellowship with the whole Trinity. All nations are to be baptized in the fullness of fellowship with the Father, Son, and the Holy Spirit. All these three dimensions of the Christian experience of God are of utmost importance to all believers. Any reduction of this experience to only one or two of its dimensions is to impoverish Christian faith. Unfortunately, this is not that rare. A few weeks ago, my wife and I attended, uh, the Sunday morning service at a well-known church in London. Throughout the service, which included quite a number of hymns, there was only one mention of the Father, and that was in the prayer of blessing at the very end of the service. But all the three distinctive features of our experience with the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit is of great significance for the Iranian church. The only God Iranians have known for centuries is more like a heavenly dictator whose only interest is to have absolute control over them. The only acceptable posture toward this god is that of a slave, in total submission. Knowing and experiencing the transcendent God who is above all his creation as a loving Father who wants to have fellowship with us as his beloved sons and daughters is such a liberating view of God and a great source of attraction to many Iranians. Knowing and experiencing the Son as he who was equal with God but did not use that for his own benefit, rather emptied himself and came among us as a human being, even as a slave, to reveal the Father to us and to die for us on the cross is such a revolutionary concept and experience of God for Iranians. Thousands have fallen in love with this God who is not just above us, but who is beside us and is standing with us in our human struggles and in our pain and suffering. The same is true with the Christian experience of the Holy Spirit as that divine person who comes and dwells within us and makes us friends of God. The Spirit is powerfully at work among Iranians in ways that reminds one of his work in the book of Acts. Experiences of the Spirit's work through dreams, visions, and miracles are among the most important reasons for the phenomenal growth of the church in Iran. Stories of such experiences go around and is drawing whole families even whole villages to Jesus. Another story that I want to share is about my own pastor. Many years he was my pastor, Edward and Anahid. Anahid, Edward's wife, was an evangelist. We have heard that she wouldn't sleep before she would speak to at least 10 people every day. So that was her joy. And one day they were going to visit a new believer in the city of Qom, that is one of the most religious cities in Iran. The Islamic seminary is located there. So as they go to visit this new believer, on the way they go to a shop to buy a bottle of water. And as they come out of the shop, they see a gentleman standing by the window of the adjacent shop. And as Anna, she saw this man, the evangelist that she was, she turns to Edward and says, "Dear Edward, I want to give our— the Gospel of John, the piece of Scripture that we have, to this gentleman who is standing there." Edward looks at this man and notices that he had a very fanatic look with full beard and the kind of dress that he was wearing. It looked like a very religious and fanatic Muslim. So Edward says to Anahid, Anahid, don't you see? Don't you see that he is clearly a fanatic Muslim? You are going to put us in trouble now. Do your evangelism somewhere else. And they got into the car and drove away. And as they were driving, after a couple of minutes, Anahit turns to Pastor Edward and says, Dear Edward, when the day comes that I stand before the judgment seat of Christ and he asks me, why didn't you give that piece of scripture to that gentleman that I sent you to? I will say Edward didn't let me do it. So argument starts coming back and forth between them, and eventually Pastor Edward gives in and says, okay, okay, we will turn around and go back, and if he's still standing there, we will give that scripture to him. So they go and the man is still there. So Anahit wants to jump out of the car gets the piece of Scripture to take to this man, and Edward says, "No, Anahid, I am going to do it. You are going to put us in trouble today." So Pastor Edward picks the Gospel of John or Matthew and goes out towards this man shaking and comes to this man, looks at him and says, "I am a Christian. I am a pastor." 'Sir, I want to give you a gift. This is a piece of Jesus' gospel, the gospel of Jesus. Would you mind if I give you this as a gift?' The man looks at Edward and tears start coming down his eyes, and Edward gets fearful and says, 'Sir, did I say something wrong? Did I offend you?' And the man says to Edward, "No, sir, you didn't say anything wrong. You see, I don't live anywhere near here. 6 months ago, I heard about Jesus from satellite TV, and I gave my life to Christ. And for 6 months, I'm looking for a piece of scripture to buy Jesus' book, and I couldn't find it anywhere." So this morning I woke up with a voice telling me, get up, get up, I'm going to take you to my servant. And I got up and the voice was telling me that go into your car, take your car and start driving. So I've been driving for an hour and as I come here, the voice says, go and stand by that window, by that shop, and I'm going to bring my servant to you. So that he will give you my book. And I've been waiting here, and when you and your wife came, the voice inside me told me that this is the— this is my servant who is going to give you my book. But you came out, and then you and your wife, you got into the car and drove away. And I was so sad because I thought maybe all that I heard It was just my own hallucinations. But thank you for coming back. Thank you for bringing me the gospel. And he took the gospel, the small tract, and he start kissing the gospel as Muslims do with their scripture. And they joined the underground church. Fourth, Fourth totality, total discipleship. Jesus calls us to disciple all the nations, and that includes teaching them to obey everything that I have commanded you. The main verb in Jesus' commission is to disciple, to make disciples. This is something of great importance to our Iranian context. As we are coming from a very different worldview and system of values, there needs to be a very thorough work of discipling hundreds who are coming to Christ. And that is what we are doing at Parsons Theological Center, training leaders who can do that. As the Christian West becomes increasingly secular, the work of making disciples gains more urgency even here. We are in great danger of reducing Christian faith mainly to accepting certain beliefs or having certain experiences. But Jesus calls us to make disciples of all the nations. The problem with lack of proper discipleship is that Christian faith can easily be turned into a consumer religion. We come to Christ only to receive something from him. Whether that something is of material value or something of a more spiritual nature, we ourselves are at the center and God is at our service. This is a great danger for the Iranian church. In such consumer religion, God himself becomes a commodity that we consume. We pull him into the very small world of our own dreams and goals rather than responding to his call of taking up our crosses, dying to self, and following him in his great story of saving and renewing the whole creation. We are to call the nations to a total commitment to Jesus as Lord. Being a disciple is about obeying him as our Lord in every area of our individual and social life. It is about spreading his gospel, his love, and his kingdom values everywhere. We cannot separate Jesus himself from his teaching and commandments. We will be fools to say that Jesus is our Savior and Lord and ignore what he has taught us. The cost of discipleship becomes such a key ingredient in Jesus's version of the Christian faith. That is something that Iranian Christians must face every day. As I said, since 2013, all the Persian-speaking churches that are from a Muslim background are shut down. Believers from that background are not allowed to gather for worship even in house groups. If found to have left Islam, they may easily lose their jobs, be expelled from college, and be taken for interrogation. And as I said, leaders of house churches, if caught, receive long jail sentences, are humiliated, beaten up, and put into solitary confinement for weeks and months. But amid all this persecution, the church continues to grow. The reason is that Iranian Christians have to count the price of following Jesus from day one. Many of our students who are leaders in the underground church in Iran go through such experiences, but Jesus's presence is with them in the most difficult circumstances. One of our students was taken to jail twice, the second time for 3 years. And a clergyman used to come and visit them. It was him and a few others together in a group. And this Muslim clergyman was coming to talk to them every 2 weeks and trying to bring them back to Islam. So after some time, a kind of friendship developed between them.. And then this clergyman told this group the last time that he visited them, said, what do you want me to bring for you? I'm going out, and so if you like something, if you like some food or something that I can bring for you, please tell me. And they immediately responded, bring us a Bible. And this clergyman is taken aback and He is scared and said, but you know, I come here to talk to you about Islam and it will be very dangerous for me to bring a Bible to you, but let me see what I can do. So he goes and after 2 weeks he comes back and he has a book covered in newspaper under his robe and comes to them and opens it up and it's an English version, English King James Version. Brings it to these students of ours in prison and he says, "I'm so sorry, I didn't find anything else. This is all that I found." But they said, "Praise the Lord!" They were so excited to have this English translation of the Bible, this archaic translation, and they took it and they started reading. And one of them knew English well. And what they did, they started translating bits and pieces from this Bible. And they were writing it on small pieces and distributing these pieces in prison. And later when we heard about this, we called the translation. They did the whole Mark and Matthew and Romans and a few of the Psalms in prison on these pieces. We called it the prison version of the Bible. So God helps and God supports us when we go on this mission, when we face hardship, when we experience difficult situations. The fifth and last totality that I want to share is about this presence of Jesus, total presence. "Surely I am with you always," or in Greek says, "every day to the very end of the age." Jesus' promise to the church he sends out is to be with them every single day to the end of time. The promise of Jesus's presence is for the Church that takes his mission seriously. Jesus's ascension does not mean that he will be absent from the Church. The opposite is in fact true. Jesus goes to the Father so that he could be present to his Church in the totality of space and time. This is the New Testament equivalent of God sending his servants on very difficult missions. God made the same promise to Moses, to Joshua, to Jeremiah, and to others that he will be with them in those difficult missions. The church's mission today, too, is not going to be an easy task. But the same God that fulfilled his promise to Moses and these other servants of him is faithful and is going to be with us wherever we go. The book of Acts shows us how Jesus fulfills this promise in the life and mission of his church. On the day of Pentecost, Jesus bestows the Spirit and the Spirit's gifts on the church from the right-hand side of the Father and is then portrayed throughout Acts as being actively present in the mission of his Church. He shows himself and he speaks to his servants several times in visions and dreams. He appears to Stephen at his martyrdom, hearing his prayer addressed to Jesus on his knees and receiving his Spirit. Similar examples are found in the risen Lord's commissioning of Ananias to go and pray for Paul in chapter 9, and in his appearing in visions and dreams to commission, strengthen, instruct, and encourage Paul. Several times Jesus shows himself to Paul and speaks to him. Acts also portrays the risen Christ as the source behind the church's preaching wisdom and miraculous work. The longer and very old ending of Mark neatly summarizes this active presence of the risen Lord with his church in mission. I'm going to read this bit from Mark 16:19 onwards. After the Lord Jesus had spoken to them, he was taken up into heaven and he sat at the right hand of God. Then the disciples went out and preached everywhere, and the Lord worked with them and confirmed his word by the signs that accompanied it. So well expressed. What we see of Jesus's presence with his church's mission in Acts is happening right now in Iran. You can hardly find any Iranian Christian that have not encountered Jesus himself in some dream and vision somewhere in their journey of faith. Many are coming to Christ through such experiences. I have just come from Canada having a conference for our students in Vancouver, and one of our students shared this about his father. His father was a drug addict for many years, and this student of ours were praying for his father for some time. And one day he comes home and sees his elderly father sitting at the stairs, on the stairs, crying. And he goes to his father and says, Dad, what is happening? What's wrong with you? What happened? Please tell me. And the father says, 'No, no, I can't, I can't share this with you. If I share it with you, you think I am high and I have used drugs or I am hallucinating and these things. I can't, I can't share it with you.' And the son insists and says, 'No, please, please tell me what happened.' And he says that, 'I came and I was taking a shower and then suddenly Jesus revealed himself. Jesus appeared to me while I was taking the shower and was washing me and told me that, "I am washing you from your sins and from your drug addiction." And I was so embarrassed under the shower when he appeared to me, and I tried to cover myself. And then Jesus told me, "Don't be shy, don't be embarrassed. I am your Creator. Why are you embarrassed of me? I have created your body. I know you so well. I am going to wash you from your addiction." And this man was so transformed and so started talking to people about what happened to him. He has a, like, Uber kind of taxi and hangs the cross on his mirror. And then people get curious and ask him, what is this cross? It seems that you are a Christian. He says, I don't know. I don't know what being a Christian means, but this has happened to me. Jesus has saved me. Jesus has changed me. If you want to know more about him, I have a booklet here I can give to you. And he is sharing about Jesus and about what he has done for him. So I finish by summarizing what I said. The same Jesus is today sending his church, is sending us on his total mission. He still has all the authority in heaven and on earth, still sends us to make disciples of all the nations. To go out of this church, you have all of them close by. He asks us again to baptize them into the fullness of fellowship with the Triune God. And he wants us to teach them to follow all that he has commanded us. And he is still promising to be with us to the end of time. Let's pray. Heavenly Father, we thank you for your total mission. We thank you for the honor of being your servants and for sending us to all the nations. We thank you for your promise to be with us, Lord. We thank you for what you are doing everywhere, what you are doing in Iran and in Uruguay and in other places, in India. And you are the same Jesus. You are doing the same kind of things. Encourage us, encourage this church that for years has been a witness for you. Encourage every one of us to speak, to speak the message that you have given us to the nations. In Jesus' name, amen. Amen.
